memory_update.text: HSTM is the cleanest underfollowed public candidate for licensure-and-simulation infrastructure because it combines healthcare learning, credentialing, competency, clinical development, resuscitation, and clinical-rotation workflows in a sub-$1B market-cap software company.
CAE is a useful reference name for healthcare simulation equipment and center infrastructure, but healthcare exposure must be sized because the company is broader than this node.
LOPE and ATGE are not suppliers; they are demand-side operators whose ABSN, pre-licensure nursing, clinical hub, and simulation-lab expansion may reveal where the bottleneck sits.

Several highly relevant licensure/simulation vendors appear private or non-US-listed, including Laerdal, Gaumard, UWorld, Prometric, Ascend Learning, TrueLearn, Exam Master, Assessment Systems, DiaMedical, and Lumis; later layers should map these as private chokepoint comparables or suppliers/customers to public companies.

summary: Expanded the universe around healthcare licensure, credentialing, clinical simulation, competency assessment, and physical-placement constraints. The strongest underfollowed public-market fit is HealthStream, which sits directly in healthcare workforce learning, credentialing, competency, and simulation-management software. CAE is the main public reference name for physical healthcare simulation equipment but is not pure-play because aviation/defense dominate. Grand Canyon Education and Adtalem are not suppliers; they are scaled education operators whose growth may reveal demand for simulation labs, licensure pathways, and scarce clinical-placement infrastructure.
